gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tamil-suppleme: Crowded, retro, and loud: Styro packs its letters tight. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement relaxes into round, parenthesis-like curves and a tall middle band, so paragraphs would read sturdy and unhurried.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Retro Styro crowds its letters until the gaps nearly vanish. Noto Sans Thai Looped has tall bodies and spacious gaps at curve terminals, so extended text would feel open yet sturdy.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Styro is tight, retro, and unmistakably loud. Noto Sans Ugaritic opens every mouth wide like an unjoined chalk arc, and that crowded-versus-open split is what makes the pairing work.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Retro Styro squeezes its letters nearly shut. Noto Sans Warang Citi lets words sit as solid blocks with wide channels into each counter, so the heading's tightness gets room to breathe beside it.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-squa: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square stands tall, with a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square opens up exactly where Styro closes in, and that's the draw.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Retro Styro is tight, crowded, and commanding. Noto Traditional Nushu follows a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, and if Styro shrank small its crowded letters would clog.
gen-fs-styro-gf-numans: Crowded letters, pressed nearly shut, are Styro's signature, giving it a retro, commanding look. Numans goes the opposite way, with widely spaced tracking and an s whose ends hang far from the spine.
gen-fs-styro-gf-onest: Crowded and retro, Styro presses its letters so close that the openings nearly disappear into tight, commanding blocks. Onest keeps big bowls and curves that never thin, the sharpest contrast.
gen-fs-styro-gf-puritan: Retro Styro crowds its letters tightly, leaving almost no gap in any curve. Puritan, rounded and oversized in its counters, gives the page somewhere to breathe whenever Styro takes over the headline.
gen-fs-styro-gf-sarpanch: Styro is retro and commanding, with letters pressed nearly shut. Sarpanch follows with a clearly open mouth on its e and a compact ascender gap, so heading and text feel like different voices.
